Controls an AMBEO Soundbar **Max, Plus or Mini** over your local network (no cloud).
The Plus is the reference model; Mini and Max are supported the same way.

## Setup

1. Find the soundbar's IP address (Smart Control app or your router).
2. Enter it in the integration's **Configuration** screen.
3. Press **Test the connection**: it reads the soundbar now and says what it
   answered (model, firmware, number of inputs, volume). If it reports an error,
   the address is wrong or the soundbar is not reachable on its port 80.
4. Run a device scan: one device with all settings your model supports is created.

## Device features

Power, volume, mute, input, sound profile, night mode, AMBEO mode, voice enhancement,
sound feedback, subwoofer, LED/logo/display brightness, Bluetooth pairing, eco mode,
audio codec and now playing (read-only). Plus and Mini also expose the center volume;
the Max exposes the AMBEO level and the center/side/up-firing levels instead.

Power follows the model: the Max can be woken from standby and put back, the button
of the widget is hidden on the other models.

A model that does not answer a whole group of settings (some firmware versions do not)
still appears: what it does not answer is logged and skipped.

## Widget "Soundbar remote"

Power on/off, volume down/up (step configurable), mute, and one button per selectable
input.

## Scenes

**Action "Read the soundbar state"** returns volume, mute, input, sound profile and
codec, readable by the following steps as `{{outputs.<key>}}`.

**Action "Set the soundbar volume"** sets an absolute volume.

**Trigger "Volume crossed a limit"** fires when the volume goes above the "too loud"
limit or below the "too quiet" limit set in the configuration. The trigger carries
the direction, the limit and the new volume. It fires once per crossing: for a plain
"volume above X" condition, use Gladys' own "device state changed" trigger on the
volume feature.

## Notes

The soundbar API is not officially documented; the paths follow the open-source
pyambeo library.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Sennheiser AMBEO Soundbar asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Soundbar IP address | `string` | Yes | IP address or hostname of the soundbar (shown in the Smart Control app or your router). |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the soundbar state is read, in seconds (one minute minimum). |
| Widget volume step | `number` | No | Volume units added or removed by the Louder / Quieter buttons. |
| Too loud above | `number` | No | Fires the 'volume crossed a limit' trigger when the volume goes above this value. 0 disables it. |
| Too quiet below | `number` | No | Fires the 'volume crossed a limit' trigger when the volume drops below this value. 0 disables it. |

## How to install Sennheiser AMBEO Soundbar in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Sennheiser AMBEO Soundbar appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/tomgermany/gladys-sennheiser-ambeo:1.1.4`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/tomgermany/gladys-sennheiser-ambeo](https://github.com/tomgermany/gladys-sennheiser-ambeo).

Sennheiser AMBEO Soundbar requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Sennheiser AMBEO Soundbar is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [tomgermany](https://github.com/tomgermany), not by the Gladys core team.
